St. Simeon the God-receiver

Saints

St. Simeon the God-receiver

St. Symeon the God-receiver

Period
At the Meeting of Christ in the Temple
Region
Holy Land
Titles / vocation
Prophet · Lay
Commemoration
February 3

Introduction

Luke describes the righteous St. Simeon recognizing Christ in the Temple; the OCA commemorates him after the Meeting of the Lord.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Death at great age in the published tradition; Scripture does not give the circumstances.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The life adds a tradition identifying St. Simeon with the translators of the Septuagint and his waiting for the fulfillment of Isaiah’s prophecy.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3

Life and notable events

The Gospel gives his encounter with the infant Christ, his blessing, and his prophecy to Mary; these events are quoted directly below.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 4 · [2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 2:25–35 (KJV)

And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord;

(As it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;)

And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.

And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him.

And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.

And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law,

Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said,

Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:

For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,

Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people;

A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.

And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.

And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against;

(Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 2: 21–35

Death and martyrdom

The OCA account reports death at a great age, traditionally360, and the later translation of relics. The extraordinary age is not given in Luke.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 8; Published biographical account,paragraph 9 · [2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 2:25–35 (KJV)

Writings and legacy

His Gospel canticle is preserved in Luke2. The source distinguishes the biblical encounter from its expanded traditions about his earlier life.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 7; Published biographical account,paragraph 8 · [2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 2:29–35 (KJV)

And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity;

And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.

And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Luke 2: 36–38

Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

Isaiah’s prophecy in the KJV; the life’s Septuagint-translator story is later tradition, not narrated by Isaiah or Luke.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Isaiah 7: 14

Chronology

  1. Before the Meeting

    Luke describes a just and devout man awaiting consolation.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 6

  2. The Meeting

    St. Simeon receives the infant Christ.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 4; Published biographical account,paragraph 9

  3. Sixth century,in the life

    Relics are reported transferred to Constantinople.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 9
